football_evidence.question: Can Utah contain Cincinnati’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Utah, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 3.7 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Cincinnati has the ball (big plays through the air): Cincinnati’s offense turns 7.7% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Utah’s defense gives up explosive gains on 8.9% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).
When Utah has the ball (third down): Utah’s offense converts 53.4% of its third downs, and Cincinnati’s defense allows opponents to convert 43.1% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).

When Utah has the ball (big plays on the ground): Utah’s offense turns 10.1% of its runs into explosive gains, and Cincinnati’s defense gives up explosive gains on 6.5% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Cincinnati has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Cincinnati’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 16.1% of its runs, and Utah’s defense stops 23.0% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
contradicting: In his last two games (West Virginia and Texas Tech), French averaged 9.4 yards per attempt, against 7.2 in his five games before that.
In his last two games (Utah State and Kansas), Ficklin averaged 8.8 yards per attempt, against 11.1 in his two games before that.
When Cincinnati has the ball (the red zone): Cincinnati’s offense succeeds on 58.5% of its red-zone plays, and Utah’s defense allows success on 35.5% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).
In his last two games (Colorado and Houston), Dampier averaged 7.2 yards per attempt, against 8.7 in his five games before that.
quarterbacks: JC French IV has completed 122 of 179 passes (68.2%) for 1,418 yards, 7.9 yards per attempt, 12 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in seven games for Cincinnati, and has been sacked on 13 of 192 dropbacks.
Devon Dampier has completed 136 of 199 passes (68.3%) for 1,625 yards, 8.2 yards per attempt, 15 touchdowns and 6 interceptions in seven games for Utah, and has been sacked on 10 of 209 dropbacks.
Byrd Ficklin has completed 10 of 18 passes (55.6%) for 186 yards, 10.3 yards per attempt, 2 touchdowns and no interceptions in four games for Utah, and has been sacked on 0 of 18 dropbacks.
